panels.visual: Ariadne in the maze-like palace corridors, young, clever, holding a ball of red thread, Daedalus the inventor in the background
panels.caption: Daedalus built the Labyrinth so cleverly that once inside you could not find the way out.

panels.visual: Ariadne handing Theseus a ball of red thread at the door of the Labyrinth, whispering
panels.caption: Ariadne loved Theseus, and gave him a ball of thread.

speech.speaker: Ariadne
speech.text: Tie the end at the door.

panels.visual: Theseus walking into the dark winding corridors, red thread unrolling behind him through the dark, torch in hand
panels.caption: He tied the end at the door and let it unroll as he walked deeper in.

panels.visual: A bird's-eye view of a maze with a single red line winding through it, a tiny hero at the centre
panels.caption: Not even Daedalus was sure he could find the way out.

panels.visual: Deep in the dark Labyrinth: the Minotaur, a massive bull-headed giant with bloodshot glowing eyes, flared steaming nostrils, nose ring, looms out of the blackness; in the foreground Theseus seen from behind, sword in hand, a red thread trailing
panels.caption: Follow the thread.

panels.visual: The Minotaur charging at Theseus, speed lines, stone walls cracking, Theseus ready with a sword, dust cloud hiding the clash; no gore
panels.caption: He found the Minotaur in the dark and killed it.

panels.visual: Two small inset pictures side by side: Theseus with his bare hands, and Theseus with a sword; a big question mark between them
panels.caption: With his bare hands, or with a sword. The stories disagree.

panels.visual: Theseus following the red thread back out of the Labyrinth to a bright doorway, Ariadne waiting with open arms in the light
panels.caption: Then he followed the thread back out to the light.
